reviews.author: gangsta
reviews.text:
I went on a date on Sharosu-gil (hahahaha) It's been a while since I found a bar at the entrance to Seoul National University with a nice atmosphere, and it's Ijinkan. It's already known as a hot place in Hongdae and Itaewon. It's a place that combines izakaya and Western style, so it'll get your emotions flowing. I'd like to recommend it as one of the few places in the area that's open until sunrise :)
​
As soon as the door opens, a purple ? The first impression was of the hazy lights softly lighting up the interior! It was a place known for its pride in its menus being made with carefully selected ingredients and handmade! You can taste the fresh raw fish you've been waiting for, and you can choose from a variety of stir-fried and fried dishes to suit your taste. There are also a variety of drinks available. It's cheaper than other places, including soju, beer, sake, and highball★ I noticed that the menu is very well prepared for those who like to mix things up!
​
Ijinkan #Sukiyaki 24,000 won
Nabe is also the representative menu here. Seeing as you gave it a name, you must be that confident, right? There is a rumor that it hit Korea's taste buds right away. It is said to be a taste that you will never forget once you eat it. They put the sukiyaki on a portable burner and took the lid right away. Once boiled, the size of the tip is quite large and the portion is generous. There is also a generous amount of ingredients!
​
​Soon after, the table was filled with shisamo grill. Now that you’re side by side, you don’t feel lonely anymore, do you, Nabeya? The two of us are eating together, but the snacks seem to be more than the alcohol. I ended up drinking about two bottles that day, so I wonder if it's the right amount. It's really filling and it's not enough for a meal.
​
#Grilled Sisamo 16,000 won
Who likes eating fish with bones? At first, I looked at the name and asked what the menu was, and it was a bit like sandfish/seaweed. Actually, I don't know exactly what the difference is, but if you grill it like this according to the season, it's delicious - how can you not eat sisamo? How do you eat this sisamo, which can be easily held in one hand? All you have to do is mix the mayonnaise sauce that comes with it, then dip it in and chew it. .. It’s a honey snack that goes really well with mayonnaise. I recommend it.
​
The atmosphere is good, the food is delicious, and the service is great~
I recommend Ijinkan for a date on Sharosu-gil ♣

reviews.text: Seongmin lamb skewers are quite well known in Korea. It is a Chinese restaurant that opened in Bongcheon-dong in 2007. It is said that the name of the store was borrowed from the name of his nephew, Seongmin, who was born in 2007. The name is Seongmin Lamb Skewers, but a variety of Chinese dishes are prepared, including ‘lamb skewers’ and ‘lamb ribs.’ But no matter what, the representative menu of Lamb Skewers Restaurant, Bongcheon-dong Restaurant, and Seoul National University Station Restaurant Seongmin Lamb Skewers is, as the name suggests, lamb skewers. If you order one serving, you will receive ten lamb skewers. The lamb skewers here are popular among men and women as they capture the unique smell of lamb well. After grilling lamb skewers over hot coals, you can enjoy a savory and soft taste by dipping them in a ‘powder sauce’ made by mixing a spice called tziran, sesame seeds, perilla seeds, and red pepper powder. Jisamseon, a Chinese-style sweet and sour pork and stir-fried vegetable dish called kkwabarou, is also popular. Unlike the long-shaped sweet and sour pork, the wide-shaped kwabarou boasts a chewy texture and sweet taste. Lamb Skewers Restaurant, Bongcheon-dong Restaurant, and Seoul National University Station Restaurant Seongmin Lamb Skewers, which opened its second branch on the first and second floors, are said to have Chinese-style decorations imported from Incheon Chinatown inside, and the colors of the tables and chairs are unified to create a clean atmosphere. ‘Chaiseon Yei’ hanging on one wall is said to be a portrait of ‘a god symbolizing wealth and fortune’ and was brought directly from a temple in China. Lamb skewers are said to protect the five intestines, control dizziness and blood pressure, and are effective in treating diabetes, intestinal dehydration, skin beauty, skin recovery, lack of energy, and osteoporosis. It is said to have lower calories and cholesterol than beef or pork. It is said that the Cheongdo lamb skewers, which I often stop by whenever I go to Yeongdeungpo, were prepared by someone who learned to cook here.

One-line review: A space like a ray of light falling on a barren land where it is hard to find baguettes other than Paris Baguette.

It's a brunch shop located in a quiet alley behind Uneun-dong... Is it true that it's fully booked within 5 minutes of opening?!?!? (After all, popular houses are less affected by the coronavirus...🧐) The small interior (up to 12 people can dine at 3 tables), vintage furniture and a cream-colored atmosphere are combined in a nonchalant manner...

These days, they provide coffee using a drip filter machine, which is hard to find in Korea. It's nice to taste it after a long time and it's good because it's delicious ^^ (Even at Byeoldabang Kongdabang, if you want to order the coffee of the day... they always say "It takes over 10 minutes to brew, are you okay?" and they show off that they don't like it... so it's hard to drink😭... haha)
About 70% of the jambon beur sandwiches are baguettes that are baked in person? Beurre and fig jam seem to have done the rest. The combination of the well-balanced, chewy baguette on the outside and the contents was great.
Other than that, the rest of the dishes (Shakshuka - spicy eaters need to be careful!! menu & chili cheese) felt relatively ordinary.

This place is recognized as a baguette restaurant!! If you're looking for a baguette sandwich near Seoldae entrance, you'll definitely come here.

p.s. Parking was taken care of, but it was disappointing that the bgm volume was a bit loud compared to the small and resonant space...🤗

There is a menu at the entrance of the store so you can look at it before entering. Ordering is done through a kiosk, so you have to choose a menu in advance.

When ordering through a kiosk, they often call out your order number, but here, the kiosk has a vibrating bell attached to it.

A single burger costs 6,700 won, and the bread and meat are delicious, but the portion is small. The contents include a meat patty, cheese, and a very small amount of onion that appears slightly pickled after being stir-fried in sauce. It feels like the bread, meat, and cheese are all there is to it, but the meat and bread themselves are delicious.

French fries (2,900 won for individual order) are also small in quantity, but they are hot and delicious compared to other franchises as they are freshly fried.

If you think about the taste alone, it is definitely delicious, but the portion is small. They didn't raise the price too much, but it felt like they reduced the quantity, so I'm satisfied with having tried it once.

I think it would be a good idea for those with a small amount of food to go.

#Life fed by the Lord #Bagel Stove

[🥯Bagel brunch cafe with a spoonful of Instagrammable food]

Let me introduce you to a bagel brunch cafe located on Sharosu-gil.
It is a sister brand of Ramiscone, a famous scone restaurant, and is located in the same building as Ramiscone on Sharosu-gil (!)
They say you can use a bagel stove on the 1st floor and a Lamis cone on the 2nd floor.
It is located about 9 minutes away from Exit 2 of Seoul National University Station, and there was no wait when I visited on a weekday evening.

First of all, as you can see in the picture, I ordered the ‘Green Onion Cream Cheese Bagel Sandwich’ on a platter, which looked really good. If you order as a platter, you get a generous meal like [Bagel Sandwich + Potato Fries + Grilled Vegetables + Cheese Dipping, Onion White Sauce + Carrot Lappé]. If you don't need this set, I recommend ordering it as a single. (I'm going to order a single next time hehe)

The bagel I chose was made with 🥬🧅 chives, onions, cream cheese, and matcha, so it was good because it felt less greasy! The cream cheese is really thick, but the chives and onions seem to cut down on the greasiness a bit. It was a taste that any Korean would like. It didn't taste like "Wow, that's crazy!", but the combination of a chewy bagel and soft cream cheese was okay. Perhaps because they bake their own bagels on the second floor, the bread is really chewy!💚

And since I was bored just eating bagels(?), I also ordered soufflé, omelette, pasta, and cream curry. Big size soufflé is visually GOOD! The spicy curry pasta was also delicious! I recommend the pasta + bagel combination.

I ordered a vanilla latte and it tasted okay.

A bagel stove that takes great photos~ Instagram-worthy photos come out really well. The price is around 10,000 won per menu.

If you are looking for a brunch cafe with good photos near Seoul National University Station, I highly recommend it.
Parking is not available, so we recommend parking in a nearby public parking lot or at the Gwanak-gu Office.

reviews.author: HaeYi
reviews.text:
This cafe was originally famous for its soufflé pancakes, so I highly recommend trying it if it’s your first time visiting. It's pretty to look at and tastes good, so I feel good when I eat it. Personally, I'm disappointed that the drinks don't seem to have much special features.
If I had to choose my top pick, it would definitely be the Acai Bowl.
It's a dish I really like, but it's hard to find nearby, so I was very happy when I found it here, and I was even more satisfied because it was reasonably priced (that doesn't mean it's cheap, though. It's about 10,000 won).
